facts.fact: The plan, dated May 2016 and prefaced by Prime Minister Philemon Yang as head of government, is called the adopted strategic plan in its monitoring section, with no adopting act named; it covers the digital economy, public administration and enterprises across all ministries.
The plan states its implementation is scheduled over five years, 2016-2020, with targets set for 2020.
The document is the plan's own full text, 72 pages, published on the MINPOSTEL site and a Cameroonian PDF copy.

The priority action plan lists projects per axis with baseline and 2020 target values, indicators, responsible bodies, priority and an amount in FCFA per project, for example 125,000,000,000 for a broadband backbone extension and 4,610,693,008 for a subscriber identification platform.

The plan assigns delivery to MINPOSTEL with the other ministries, ANTIC, ART and CAMTEL, and assigns monitoring and evaluation to the PPBS committees of each administration and their monitoring-evaluation cells.

The plan's financing column ties projects to domestic lines (BIP, the public investment budget, FST, the telecommunications special fund, and Budget de l'Etat) alongside FINEX external financing and some projects marked as funding sought.
